sentences.en: At the first gray of dawn, with a heavy heart, I got into the motor car and drove out to the prison.
sentences.zh: 黎明破晓时分，我怀着沉重的心情坐进汽车，驶向监狱。

sentences.en: I sent in my name to Miss Carville.
sentences.zh: 我让人通报了我的名字，求见卡维尔小姐。

sentences.en: If I remember rightly, the soldier told me she had just been kneeling at her table.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，士兵告诉我她刚才还跪在桌前。

sentences.en: In the cell, a flickering gas flame was burning.
sentences.zh: 牢房里，一盏煤气灯在闪烁。

sentences.en: Two large bouquets of wizard flowers, which had been standing there for ten weeks, wakened the impression of a vault.
sentences.zh: 两束巨大的巫师花已经在那里放了十周，让人感觉像是在墓穴里一样。

sentences.en: The condemned lady had packed all her little property, its greatest care, in a handbag.
sentences.zh: 这位被判死刑的女士把她所有的细软——她最珍视的东西——都装进了一个手提包里。

sentences.en: I accompanied her through the long corridors of the great prison.
sentences.zh: 我陪着她走过大监狱漫长的走廊。

sentences.en: The Belgian prison officials stood there and greeted her silently, with the highest respect.
sentences.zh: 比利时狱警站在那里，默默地向她致意，神情极其恭敬。

sentences.en: She returned their greetings silently.
sentences.zh: 她也默默地回礼。

sentences.en: And we boarded the motor car, which awaited us in the yard.
sentences.zh: 我们登上了在院子里等候的汽车。

sentences.en: And I sat beside Edith Carville, in order to accompany her to her own burial.
sentences.zh: 我坐在伊迪丝·卡维尔身边，陪她走完通往她自己葬礼的最后一段路。

sentences.en: So that was the German pastor, Paul Lasseur, who was chaplain at the great prison of St. Gilles in Brussels.
sentences.zh: 以上就是德国牧师保罗·拉瑟尔的叙述，他当时是布鲁塞尔圣吉尔大监狱的随军牧师。

sentences.en: And in that passage, he is recalling the last hours of a British nurse called Edith Carville,
sentences.zh: 在那段文字中，他回忆了一位名叫伊迪丝·卡维尔的英国护士的最后时刻，

sentences.en: who was about to be executed by a German firing squad for war treason on the 12th of October, 1915.
sentences.zh: 她因战时叛国罪，于1915年10月12日被德国行刑队处决。

sentences.en: And if you're wondering how a British nurse can be executed by the Germans for treason, well, we will be coming to that.
sentences.zh: 如果你想知道一位英国护士怎么会被德国人以叛国罪处决，别急，我们稍后会讲到。

sentences.en: And, Dominic, you think that her life and death is one of the most moving stories of the entire First World War.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你认为她的一生和结局是整个第一次世界大战中最动人的故事之一。

sentences.en: And you were just saying how you wish that you had had the chance to talk about it with her.
sentences.zh: 你刚才还说，真希望有机会能和她聊聊。

sentences.en: She would be high on your list of dinner party guests.
sentences.zh: 她一定是你晚宴宾客名单上的首选。

sentences.en: Because it is an amazing story, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为这确实是一个了不起的故事，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's a story of spying and resistance and of courage and treachery and of patriotism and faith.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于间谍活动、抵抗运动、勇气、背叛、爱国主义和信仰的故事。

sentences.en: And she's such a fascinating character that it would make a really brilliant film, you'd say.
sentences.zh: 而且她是一个如此迷人的人物，你会说这绝对能拍成一部精彩的电影。

sentences.en: That's not right, Tom.
sentences.zh: 那可不对，汤姆。

sentences.en: No, I was actually saying something very different about it.
sentences.zh: 不，我其实对这件事有完全不同的看法。

sentences.en: I think I like a funster at a dinner party.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我喜欢晚宴上有个风趣的人。

sentences.en: And I don't think Edith Carville was...
sentences.zh: 而且我不认为伊迪丝·卡维尔是……

sentences.en: I don't think she was one of life's funsters.
sentences.zh: 我不认为她是那种生活中的开心果。

sentences.en: But a remarkable person.
sentences.zh: 但她确实是一位非凡的人。

sentences.en: She was a remarkable person and it is a truly remarkable story that we'll be talking about today.
sentences.zh: 她是一位非凡的人，我们今天所要讲述的也确实是一个非凡的故事。

sentences.en: So, as you say, it's one of the most colourful and controversial stories of the whole First World War.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这是整个第一次世界大战中最丰富多彩且最具争议的故事之一。

sentences.en: And you say here that she's probably the war's single best-known casualty after Franz Ferdinand.
sentences.zh: 你在这里提到，她可能是继弗朗茨·斐迪南之后，战争中知名度最高的受害者。

sentences.en: Well, if you think about people who were killed in the First World War, especially people who were killed while not fighting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你想到那些在第一次世界大战中丧生的人，尤其是那些并非死于战场的人。

sentences.en: Which is true, both of Franz Ferdinand and of Edith Carville.
sentences.zh: 这一点对弗朗茨·斐迪南和伊迪丝·卡维尔来说都是事实。

sentences.en: There aren't that many who have statues.
sentences.zh: 没几个人能拥有雕像。

sentences.en: Edith Carville does, of course, have a statue.
sentences.zh: 当然，伊迪丝·卡维尔有雕像。

sentences.en: She has a statue of Trafalgar Square.
sentences.zh: 她在特拉法加广场有一座雕像。

sentences.en: And every day, I guess, every year, hundreds of thousands of people must walk past that statue.
sentences.zh: 我想，每天，或者说每年，成千上万的人一定都会经过那座雕像。

sentences.en: They probably barely give it a second's thought.
sentences.zh: 他们可能连看都不会多看一眼。

sentences.en: Or they walk past the statue of her in King's Domain in Melbourne, in Australia.
sentences.zh: 或者他们会经过她在澳大利亚墨尔本国王领地的那座雕像。

sentences.en: Or they walk along one of the countless Rue Edith Cavell in France or in Belgium.
sentences.zh: 或者走过法国或比利时无数条以“伊迪丝·卡维尔”命名的街道。

sentences.en: Or the schools and hospitals that are named after her, you know, all over the world.
sentences.zh: 又或者那些以她名字命名的学校和医院，你知道，遍布世界各地。

sentences.en: In Australia, New Zealand, in Canada, in the United States, and here in Britain.
sentences.zh: 在澳大利亚、新西兰、加拿大、美国，以及我们英国本土。

sentences.en: And there was a monument to her in Paris, which no longer stands for reasons that we will be coming to you in due course.
sentences.zh: 巴黎也曾有一座纪念她的丰碑，但由于一些我们稍后会提到的原因，它已经不在了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So she became, I think, the great martyr of the First World War.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，她成为了第一次世界大战中伟大的殉道者。

sentences.en: Perhaps she's not as well known now as she used to be.
sentences.zh: 也许她现在不像过去那么出名了。

sentences.en: But the story behind her martyrdom is an interesting one, because it's a story, as we said, of espionage and secret machinations.
sentences.zh: 但她殉道背后的故事很有趣，因为正如我们所说，这是一个关于间谍活动和秘密阴谋的故事。

sentences.en: And it's a complicated story.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一个复杂的故事。

sentences.en: And let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 让我们深入了解一下。

sentences.en: We'll start with the place where it all happens.
sentences.zh: 我们从这一切发生的地方开始讲起。

sentences.en: And that is plucky little Belgium.
sentences.zh: 那就是勇敢的小比利时。

sentences.en: So people who listened to our first series about the Great War may recall that at the beginning of the war,
sentences.zh: 听过我们第一季关于“大战”节目的听众可能还记得，在战争初期，

sentences.en: Belgium resisted the German demands for free passage in August 1914.
sentences.zh: 1914年8月，比利时抵制了德国要求自由通行的要求。

sentences.en: But within weeks, Belgium was absolutely steamrollered.
sentences.zh: 但在几周之内，比利时就被彻底碾压了。

sentences.en: These extraordinary scenes of the kind of grey ranks, like a tide, like a kind of tide of Teutonic militarism pouring through the streets of Brussels.
sentences.zh: 那些非同寻常的场景，灰色的军阵如潮水般涌入布鲁塞尔的街道，那是一种条顿军国主义的浪潮。

sentences.en: Did you really just say that?
sentences.zh: 你刚才真的说了那句话吗？

sentences.en: A tide of Teutonic militarism.
sentences.zh: 条顿军国主义的浪潮。

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 我说了。

sentences.en: But you know me, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但你了解我，汤姆。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我了解。

sentences.en: I said it in a proving way.
sentences.zh: 我是带着赞许的语气说的。

sentences.en: A tidal wave of Teutonic militarism.
sentences.zh: 条顿军国主义的滔天巨浪。

sentences.en: I love a tidal wave of Teutonic.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢条顿的滔天巨浪。

sentences.en: I love a peaked helmet.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢尖顶头盔。

sentences.en: So the Germans occupied Belgium.
sentences.zh: 所以，德国人占领了比利时。

sentences.en: They executed infamously about 6,500 civilians in their reprisals against suspected partisans.
sentences.zh: 他们臭名昭著地处决了大约6500名平民，作为对疑似游击队员的报复。

sentences.en: And they burned the medieval core of the city of Louvain.
sentences.zh: 他们还烧毁了鲁汶市的中世纪核心区。

sentences.en: A library, which I know you were very shocked by, as somebody who loves libraries.
sentences.zh: 那座图书馆，我知道你作为一名爱书人，对此感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: So even before today's story begins,
sentences.zh: 所以，甚至在今天的故事开始之前，

sentences.en: people in Britain and in neutral countries and the United States and so on are primed to see Belgium as a place where Teutonic barbarians in these kind of spiked helmets are carrying out dreadful atrocities against innocent women.
sentences.zh: 英国、中立国、美国等国家的人们就已经被灌输了一种观念：比利时是一个被戴着尖顶头盔的条顿野蛮人蹂躏的地方，他们对无辜妇女犯下了可怕的暴行。

sentences.en: So already there are British posters that sort of say, remember Belgium.
sentences.zh: 所以当时已经有了英国海报，上面写着“记住比利时”。

sentences.en: And the image of Belgium as a sort of maiden being violated by slavering Huns.
sentences.zh: 还有比利时被如饥似渴的匈奴人蹂躏的少女形象。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's kind of a guerrilla, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，那有点像大猩猩，不是吗？

sentences.en: With a club holding a, like, almost like King Kong.
sentences.zh: 手里拿着一根棍子，就像金刚一样。

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Holding a maiden in its arMs.
sentences.zh: 怀里抱着一个少女。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是这样。

sentences.en: So by the end of 1914, almost all of Belgium is under military occupation.
sentences.zh: 所以到1914年底，几乎整个比利时都处于军事占领之下。

sentences.en: It's been divided into three occupation zones, and the largest of these, which includes Brussels, is called the General Government,
sentences.zh: 它被划分为三个占领区，其中最大的一个，包括布鲁塞尔，被称为“总督府”，

sentences.en: anticipating what's going to happen to Poland in the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 这预示了二战中波兰将会发生什么。

sentences.en: And here you have a German general, and he leads a German-dominated administration.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你有一位德国将军，他领导着一个以德国人为主导的行政机构。

sentences.en: And it's actually a pretty heavy-handed occupation.
sentences.zh: 而且这实际上是一场相当高压的占领。

sentences.en: So Belgium had been the world's sixth biggest economy before the war.
sentences.zh: 要知道，战前比利时曾是世界第六大经济体。

sentences.en: So much for plucky little Belgium.
sentences.zh: 勇敢的小比利时也不过如此。

sentences.en: But the Germans dismantle the Belgian economy.
sentences.zh: 但德国人拆解了比利时的经济。

sentences.en: I mean, they basically move loads of machinery and equipment to Germany, and they deport more than 100,000 Belgian workers to German war factories.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们基本上把大量的机械设备运往德国，并将超过10万名比利时工人强行遣送到德国的军工厂。

sentences.en: They even demand that the Belgians shift their time zone.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至要求比利时人更改时区。

sentences.en: So by an hour, from GMT to Central European time.
sentences.zh: 将时间拨快一小时，从格林威治标准时间改为中欧时间。

sentences.en: And for ordinary Belgians, these are grim years, the years of occupation.
sentences.zh: 对于普通比利时人来说，这些是阴暗的岁月，是占领的岁月。

sentences.en: It's maybe not like being occupied by Nazi Germany, but there's a sense of national humiliation.
sentences.zh: 也许不像被纳粹德国占领那样，但有一种民族屈辱感。

sentences.en: There's an economic collapse.
sentences.zh: 经济崩溃了。

sentences.en: There are massive food shortages.
sentences.zh: 食物极度短缺。

sentences.en: One way that Belgians deal with this, I mean, Belgium is a very Catholic country.
sentences.zh: 比利时人应对这种情况的一种方式——我的意思是，比利时是一个非常虔诚的天主教国家。

sentences.en: It's how they define themselves against their neighbours in the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们区别于邻国荷兰的方式。

sentences.en: And there's a sort of revival of Catholicism, which actually plays a part in today's story.
sentences.zh: 天主教有一种复兴，这实际上在今天的故事中发挥了作用。

sentences.en: And the other way they respond, of course, is by resistance.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们应对的另一种方式就是抵抗。

sentences.en: And we shall be coming to this exactly how the Belgians resiSt.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会讲到比利时人究竟是如何抵抗的。

sentences.en: But resistance is where today's heroine, Edith Cavill, comes in.
sentences.zh: 但抵抗正是今天的主人公伊迪丝·卡维尔登场的地方。

sentences.en: And she, I have to say, is a very, very unlikely Belgian resistance hero.
sentences.zh: 而且我必须说，她是一个非常、非常不可能成为比利时抵抗英雄的人。

sentences.en: So she's a Victorian, born in 1865 in a village outside Norwich called Swardeston.
sentences.zh: 她是一位维多利亚时代的人，1865年出生在诺里奇郊外一个叫斯沃德斯顿的村庄。

sentences.en: And her father was the vicar there.
sentences.zh: 她的父亲是那里的牧师。

sentences.en: He was called Frederick Cavill.
sentences.zh: 他叫弗雷德里克·卡维尔。

sentences.en: He was the vicar there for almost half a century.
sentences.zh: 他在那里担任了近半个世纪的牧师。

sentences.en: He was like Nelson's dad.
sentences.zh: 他就像纳尔逊的父亲一样。

sentences.en: Yes, except he's more formidable.
sentences.zh: 是的，只不过他更令人生畏。

sentences.en: Nelson's dad was a little bit, was mild-mannered and easygoing.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊的父亲有点温和随和。

sentences.en: A bit wet, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 有点软弱，不是吗？

sentences.en: This bloke's not wet at all.
sentences.zh: 这家伙一点也不软弱。

sentences.en: He's a sort of terrifying Victorian with massive sideburns.
sentences.zh: 他是一个留着浓密鬓角的、可怕的维多利亚时代人。

sentences.en: I mean, an indication of what kind of man her father is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从一件事可以看出她父亲是什么样的人。

sentences.en: When her father was training to become a parson, he fell in love with his housekeeper's daughter, who was called Louisa, and he wanted to marry her.
sentences.zh: 当她父亲在接受牧师培训时，他爱上了管家的女儿路易莎，并想娶她。

sentences.en: But he said to her, I will only marry you when you've educated yourself to an appropriate level for a parson's wife.
sentences.zh: 但他对她说：“只有当你受过足够的教育，达到牧师妻子的标准时，我才会娶你。”

sentences.en: And depending, you know, some people may say that's unromantic of him.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能会说他太不浪漫了。

sentences.en: Others may applaud his high standards.
sentences.zh: 另一些人可能会赞赏他的高标准。

sentences.en: I leave that to the listeners to decide.
sentences.zh: 我留给听众去评判。

sentences.en: But anyway, this bloke gets a living in Norfolk, and that's where Edith is born, where she grows up.
sentences.zh: 总之，这家伙在诺福克谋得了一个职位，伊迪丝就是在那儿出生并长大的。

sentences.en: It's obviously an austere kind of existence.
sentences.zh: 那显然是一种苦行僧般的生活。

sentences.en: So they had servants, and one anecdote we have about the servants is that a maid wants scrawled in pencil on the wall of her attic bedroom.
sentences.zh: 他们有仆人，关于仆人，我们有一个轶事：一个女仆在阁楼卧室的墙上用铅笔潦草地写道：

sentences.en: The pay is small.
sentences.zh: 薪水微薄。

sentences.en: The food is bad.
sentences.zh: 食物糟糕。

sentences.en: I wonder why I don't go mad, which doesn't say much for the jollity and generosity of the Cavill family.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么我还没疯，这说明卡维尔一家并不怎么快乐和慷慨。

sentences.en: Basically, we don't really know anything about Edith when she's growing up.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我们对伊迪丝成长过程中的事情知之甚少。

sentences.en: I mean, the accounts that you find, she liked dogs, she liked ice skating, she liked flowers.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你找到的记载里说她喜欢狗，喜欢滑冰，喜欢花。

sentences.en: But this is so generic.
sentences.zh: 但这太笼统了。

sentences.en: This is so sort of generic, saintly Victorian child that I don't think you can extrapolate much from it.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常典型的、圣洁的维多利亚时代儿童形象，我认为你无法从中推断出太多东西。

sentences.en: She's educated at home at first, and she goes to a series of boarding schools.
sentences.zh: 她起初是在家里接受教育，后来上了一系列寄宿学校。

sentences.en: Her big thing at boarding school apparently was French.
sentences.zh: 她在寄宿学校最擅长的科目显然是法语。

sentences.en: She has a great gift for French.
sentences.zh: 她在法语方面很有天赋。

sentences.en: And at her school in Peterborough, they do no fewer than 10 whole minutes of French conversation every day.
sentences.zh: 在彼得伯勒的学校里，他们每天进行不少于10分钟的法语对话练习。

sentences.en: Unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 难以置信。

sentences.en: I mean, if people say that the British don't bother learning foreign languages.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果有人说英国人不屑于学习外语的话。

sentences.en: Total fluency.
sentences.zh: 完全精通。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She's a tremendous linguiSt.
sentences.zh: 她是一位了不起的语言学家。

sentences.en: She's not learning Flemish, though.
sentences.zh: 不过她没学弗拉芒语。

sentences.en: No, she's not.
sentences.zh: 不，她不是。

sentences.en: Exactly, no.
sentences.zh: 没错，不是。

sentences.en: So she works as a governess, and in 1890, she is recommended for a post in Brussels, where she goes off to work for the Francois family.
sentences.zh: 她当时担任家庭教师，1890年，她被推荐去布鲁塞尔的一个职位，于是她动身前往弗朗索瓦一家工作。

sentences.en: And what is she like?
sentences.zh: 她是个什么样的人？

sentences.en: Now, you said at the beginning that she might be a fun person to talk to at a dinner party.
sentences.zh: 你刚才开头说，她在晚宴上可能会是个有趣的聊天对象。

sentences.en: I'm not so sure.
sentences.zh: 我不太确定。

sentences.en: So the accounts that you have of her as a young woman, she's very short.
sentences.zh: 根据你手头关于她年轻时的记录，她个子非常矮。

sentences.en: I mean, that's not a reason not to talk to her at a dinner party.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这并不是在晚宴上不跟她聊天的理由。

sentences.en: But she's not at one of life's funsters and japesters.
sentences.zh: 但她绝不是那种生活中的乐天派或爱玩闹的人。

sentences.en: So a trainee nurse who's met her later said, her voice was low, agreeable, and cultured.
sentences.zh: 一位后来见过她的实习护士说，她的声音低沉、悦耳且有教养。

sentences.en: Her French fluent, which she's done 10 minutes a day.
sentences.zh: 她的法语很流利，那是她每天练习10分钟练出来的。

sentences.en: Everything around her, the neatness of her attire, her attitude and poise, the words she used, all conveyed her characteristic efficiency, thoroughness, serenity, and kindness.
sentences.zh: 她周围的一切，她着装的整洁、她的态度和仪态、她所用的词汇，都传达出她那种特有的高效、严谨、从容和善良。

sentences.en: They're not attributes that I look for in a conversationalist, frankly, but anyway.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，这些并不是我寻找聊天对象时看重的特质，但不管怎么说吧。

sentences.en: And canism at its beSt.
sentences.zh: 而且是极致的“卡维尔式”风格。

sentences.en: Obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然。

sentences.en: She has this very, very sort of Christian sensibility.
sentences.zh: 她有一种非常、非常典型的基督教情怀。

sentences.en: She wrote to her cousin,
sentences.zh: 她曾写信给她的表亲：

sentences.en: Someday I'm going to do something useful, something for people.
sentences.zh: 总有一天，我要做些有用的事，为人们做些事。

sentences.en: They're most of them so helpless, so hurt, and so unhappy.
sentences.zh: 他们大多数人都那么无助、那么受伤、那么不幸。

sentences.en: I mean, you bring her alive, you bring her alive.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你把她写活了，你把她写活了。

sentences.en: And I frankly, however short she is, I would relish the chance to spend an evening listening to her talk about flower arranging.
sentences.zh: 坦白讲，无论她个子有多矮，我都非常乐意有机会花上一晚听她谈论插花。

sentences.en: I think there's just a trace in her conversation of the Grantham grocer's shop, no?
sentences.zh: 我觉得在她的谈吐中，还是能隐约听出格兰瑟姆杂货店的影子，不是吗？

sentences.en: Of the Grantham grammar school girl who's going to lecture you about God's plans for you.
sentences.zh: 听得出那个格兰瑟姆文法学校女生的影子，她会给你讲上帝为你安排的计划。

sentences.en: Anyway, in the 1890s, she comes home from Brussels, and she ends up training as a nurse.
sentences.zh: 总之，19世纪90年代，她从布鲁塞尔回到家，最终接受了护士培训。

sentences.en: And she rises to become the assistant matron of a hospital in Shoreditch in 1903.
sentences.zh: 1903年，她晋升为肖尔迪奇一家医院的助理护士长。

sentences.en: Now, on the issue of her as a dinner party companion, I mean, I didn't think this would be such a theme of the episode, but there we are.
sentences.zh: 关于她作为晚宴同伴的问题，我没想到这会成为这集节目的主题，但事实就是这样。

sentences.en: She's very good at running this hospital, but she's not a bundle of laughs.
sentences.zh: 她非常擅长管理这家医院，但她绝不是个开心果。

sentences.en: So, these are the reports of her from the late 1890s and 1900s.
sentences.zh: 这些是19世纪90年代末到1900年代关于她的评价。

sentences.en: A very strict person who demands obedience from others.
sentences.zh: 一个非常严厉、要求他人服从的人。

sentences.en: Orderly, methodical, and of kindly and gentle disposition.
sentences.zh: 井井有条、做事有方，性格和蔼温柔。

sentences.en: Unbelievably unselfish, with an almost fanatical sense of duty.
sentences.zh: 极其无私，有一种近乎狂热的责任感。

sentences.en: Rather withdrawn, uninterested in superficial friendships, but thoughtful, pleasant, and sympathetic to all her patients.
sentences.zh: 比较内向，对肤浅的友谊不感兴趣，但对所有病人既体贴又亲切，富有同情心。

sentences.en: Does that tick your boxes, Tom?
sentences.zh: 这符合你的要求吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But anyway, in 1907, she is recruited to go back to Belgium.
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，1907年，她被招募回比利时。

sentences.en: Now, she'd been working, remember, as a governess for the Francois family.
sentences.zh: 记住，她之前一直在弗朗索瓦一家当家庭教师。

sentences.en: And they have a family friend called Dr. Antoine Depage.
sentences.zh: 他们有一位家庭朋友叫安托万·德帕日医生。

sentences.en: How familiar are you, Tom, with the history of Belgian nursing?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你对比利时护理史有多了解？

sentences.en: I'm pretty familiar.
sentences.zh: 我相当了解。

sentences.en: I mean, everyone obviously has heard of Dr. Antoine Depage.
sentences.zh: 我是说，显然每个人都听说过安托万·德帕日医生。

sentences.en: He's a name that trips off the tongue when discussing the history of Belgian nursing.
sentences.zh: 在讨论比利时护理史时，他的名字总是脱口而出。

sentences.en: I mean, if you want to go deeper into the weeds, then maybe not.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果你想深入研究细节，那可能就另当别论了。

sentences.en: But Dr. Antoine Depage, I know all about him.
sentences.zh: 但安托万·德帕日医生，我对他了如指掌。

sentences.en: Doing a bonus, surely.
sentences.zh: 肯定是在做额外功课。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Antoine Depage.
sentences.zh: 嗯，安托万·德帕日医生。

sentences.en: He's the Belgian royal surgeon, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他是比利时皇家外科医生，对吧？

sentences.en: And he's also, he's founder of the Belgian Red Cross.
sentences.zh: 他还是比利时红十字会的创始人。

sentences.en: And also, he was co-founder of the Belgian Boy Scouts.
sentences.zh: 而且，他还是比利时童子军的联合创始人。

sentences.en: And, Dominic, here's an amazing fact about him, which, of course, you will know, but probably listeners who know the outline of his life may not be aware of this.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，关于他有一个惊人的事实，当然你肯定知道，但了解他生平梗概的听众可能并不知情。

sentences.en: His daughter, Marie, died on the Lusitania.
sentences.zh: 他的女儿玛丽死在卢西塔尼亚号上。

sentences.en: Probably everyone does know that.
sentences.zh: 可能大家都知道这一点。

sentences.en: But just for the few who don't know anything about him, it's an interesting fact.
sentences.zh: 但对于那些对他一无所知的少数听众来说，这是一个有趣的事实。

sentences.en: And also, isn't it the case that he's very keen to set up Belgium's first nursing school on the outskirts of Brussels?
sentences.zh: 而且，他不是非常热衷于在布鲁塞尔郊外建立比利时第一所护士学校吗？

sentences.en: Because up until this point, nursing has been largely controlled by Catholic nuns.
sentences.zh: 因为在那之前，护理工作主要由天主教修女控制。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Dr. Antoine Depage thinks that nuns are backward and useless.
sentences.zh: 安托万·德帕日医生认为修女们思想落后且毫无用处。

sentences.en: And so he wants to bring Edith Carvel in as a matron and director.
sentences.zh: 所以他想请伊迪丝·卡维尔担任护士长和院长。

sentences.en: So, Dominic, what about Edith?
sentences.zh: 那么，多米尼克，伊迪丝怎么样？

sentences.en: How does she come in?
sentences.zh: 她是怎么加入的？

sentences.en: Dr. Depage says to her, come and set up this nursing school.
sentences.zh: 德帕日医生对她说，来创办这所护士学校吧。

sentences.en: She says, brilliant, can't wait.
sentences.zh: 她说，太棒了，迫不及待。

sentences.en: She goes over to Belgium.
sentences.zh: 她去了比利时。

sentences.en: She goes to Brussels.
sentences.zh: 她去了布鲁塞尔。

sentences.en: She sets up Belgium's first ever professional nursing journal.
sentences.zh: 她创办了比利时有史以来第一份专业护理杂志。

sentences.en: Did you know that?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: And she's so interesting, Dominic, isn't she, that she gets the second job as matron of the big new secular hospital at St. Gilles.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，她太有趣了，不是吗？她还兼任了圣吉尔大型新世俗医院的护士长。

sentences.en: It's mad that some people say she's not interesting.
sentences.zh: 有些人说她不有趣，这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: Doesn't get more interesting than that.
sentences.zh: 没有比这更有趣的了。

sentences.en: And then in 1914, she goes back in the summer, doesn't she, to Norfolk to visit her elderly mother, who's now a widow.
sentences.zh: 然后1914年夏天，她回到诺福克探望她年迈的母亲，她母亲当时已经守寡了。

sentences.en: So that's sad.
sentences.zh: 所以这很令人难过。

sentences.en: The father's dead.
sentences.zh: 父亲去世了。

sentences.en: She goes back to Norfolk.
sentences.zh: 她回到了诺福克。

sentences.en: Alan Partridge is heartland.
sentences.zh: 那是艾伦·帕特里奇的故乡。

sentences.en: And the story goes that she is weeding her mother's garden in College Road, Norwich, when she hears the news of the German invasion of Belgium.
sentences.zh: 故事是这样的，当她在诺里奇学院路的母亲花园里除草时，听到了德国入侵比利时的消息。

sentences.en: So if there was a film, this is the point at which a small child kicking a ball says, have you heard?
sentences.zh: 如果这是一部电影，这正是那个踢球的小孩跑过来说：“你听说了吗？”的时刻。

sentences.en: Germany's invaded Belgium.
sentences.zh: 德国入侵比利时了。

sentences.en: She's like, what?
sentences.zh: 她会说：“什么？”

sentences.en: And her mum says to her, don't go back, Edith.
sentences.zh: 她母亲对她说：“别回去了，伊迪丝。”

sentences.en: And Edith, because she's a saint, says, my duty is with my nurses.
sentences.zh: 而伊迪丝因为她是圣人，她说：“我的职责在于我的护士们。”

sentences.en: At a time like this, I am more needed than ever.
sentences.zh: 在这样的时刻，我比以往任何时候都更被需要。

sentences.en: Now, as this might suggest, we are very dependent for all this on incredibly treacly hagiographies that were written after her death.
sentences.zh: 正如这可能暗示的那样，我们对这一切的了解在很大程度上依赖于她死后写下的那些极其煽情的圣徒传记。

sentences.en: So whether this really happened and whether she really said this, you know, listeners can draw their own conclusions.
sentences.zh: 所以这是否真的发生过，她是否真的说过这些话，听众们可以得出自己的结论。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 总之。

sentences.en: But why otherwise would she have gone back?
sentences.zh: 但如果不这样，她为什么要回去呢？

sentences.en: I mean, it seems plausible to me.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这对我来说似乎很合理。

sentences.en: Maybe she wants to set up another nursing journal in Belgium, might become the matron of a third hospital, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 也许她想在比利时创办另一份护理杂志，可能成为第三家医院的护士长，我不知道。

sentences.en: Not with a tidal wave of grey Prussian militarism descending on her.
sentences.zh: 但当时灰色的普鲁士军国主义浪潮正向她袭来。

sentences.en: Right, a tidal wave of Teutonic militarism, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，条顿军国主义的浪潮，正是如此。

sentences.en: Anyway, by the 3rd of August, she's gone back to Brussels.
sentences.zh: 总之，到8月3日，她已经回到了布鲁塞尔。

sentences.en: She sends the German nurses that she's got home.
sentences.zh: 她把手下的德国护士送回了家。

sentences.en: She says, you can go home.
sentences.zh: 她说，你们可以回家了。

sentences.en: She says to the other nurses, your task is to care for any soldiers, regardless of their nationality.
sentences.zh: 她对其他护士说，你们的任务是照顾任何士兵，无论他们的国籍如何。

sentences.en: Any wounded soldier must be treated, friend or foe.
sentences.zh: 任何受伤的士兵都必须得到救治，无论是敌是友。

sentences.en: Every man is a father, husband or son.
sentences.zh: 每个人都是父亲、丈夫或儿子。

sentences.en: As nurses, you must take no part in the quarrel.
sentences.zh: 作为护士，你们绝不能参与争斗。

sentences.en: Our work is for humanity.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作是为了全人类。

sentences.en: The profession of nursing, there is no frontiers.
sentences.zh: 护理这一职业，是没有国界的。

sentences.en: So, 20th of August, she's been back for two weeks and Brussels falls.
sentences.zh: 所以，8月20日，她回去两周后，布鲁塞尔沦陷了。

sentences.en: And, you know, the German tidal wave trumps into the city.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，德国的浪潮冲进了城市。

sentences.en: And Edith writes in her journal, We were divided between pity for those poor fellows far from their country and their people.
sentences.zh: 伊迪丝在日记中写道：“我们内心交织着怜悯，为了那些远离家乡和亲人的可怜人。”

sentences.en: So, she's talking about the Germans there.
sentences.zh: 所以，她是在说德国人。

sentences.en: She's talking about the Germans.
sentences.zh: 她是在说德国人。

sentences.en: Suffering the weariness and fatigue of an arduous campaign.
sentences.zh: “忍受着艰苦战役带来的疲惫和劳累。”

sentences.en: This is my kind of talk.
sentences.zh: 这才是我想听的。

sentences.en: And hate of a vindictive foe bringing ruin and desolation on hundreds of happy homes and to a prosperous and peaceful land.
sentences.zh: “以及对一个复仇敌人的憎恨，它给成百上千个幸福的家庭，给这片繁荣和平的土地带来了毁灭和荒凉。”

sentences.en: Now, by this point, our training school and the sort of clinic have been converted into a Red Cross hospital.
sentences.zh: 此时，我们的培训学校和诊所已经被改造成了一家红十字医院。

sentences.en: And all English nurses have now been sent home.
sentences.zh: 所有的英国护士现在都被送回了家。

sentences.en: But Edith stays on with her assistant, who's called Miss Wilkins.
sentences.zh: 但伊迪丝和她的助手威尔金斯小姐留了下来。

sentences.en: And would I be correct in assuming that Miss Wilkins is English as well?
sentences.zh: 我假设威尔金斯小姐也是英国人，对吗？

sentences.en: Exactly, she is.
sentences.zh: 没错，她是。

sentences.en: I imagine her as having steel-rimmed spectacles.
sentences.zh: 我想象她戴着一副钢丝边眼镜。

sentences.en: Prost me.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So, then, a few weeks later comes the moment that it changes her life.
sentences.zh: 那么，几周后，改变她一生的时刻到来了。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: This is where Dr. Depage comes back.
sentences.zh: 这就是德帕日医生回来的地方。

sentences.en: So, he's the guy who first brought her to Belgium.
sentences.zh: 所以，他就是当初把她带到比利时的人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he has his daughter, Marie, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他有个女儿叫玛丽，对吧？

sentences.en: Remember what happens to Marie?
sentences.zh: 还记得玛丽发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: What happened to Marie?
sentences.zh: 玛丽发生了什么？

sentences.en: Oh, she ends up on the Lusitania.
sentences.zh: 哦，她最后上了卢西塔尼亚号。

sentences.en: But before she gets on the Lusitania, she comes to see Edith.
sentences.zh: 但在她登上卢西塔尼亚号之前，她来见了伊迪丝。

sentences.en: And says that a friend has come to ask her for help with two British soldiers.
sentences.zh: 并说有一位朋友来请她帮忙救助两名英国士兵。

sentences.en: Lieutenant Colonel Dudley Bodger and Sergeant Major Frank Meachin.
sentences.zh: 达德利·博杰中校和弗兰克·米钦军士长。

sentences.en: I think it's Dudley Boger.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是达德利·博格。

sentences.en: No?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: I can't do that.
sentences.zh: 我记不清了。

sentences.en: All these years I've been reading about this and I thought it was Bodger.
sentences.zh: 这么多年来我一直读到这个名字，我以为是博杰。

sentences.en: So, these two guys were both in the Cheshires.
sentences.zh: 所以，这两个人都是柴郡团的。

sentences.en: And they both fought in the Battle of Monge.
sentences.zh: 他们都参加了蒙斯战役。

sentences.en: Remember the Angels of Monge, Tom?
sentences.zh: 还记得蒙斯天使吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: The archers who saved the British?
sentences.zh: 那些拯救了英军的弓箭手？

sentences.en: So, they were both badly wounded in the British retreat from Mons.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们在英军从蒙斯撤退时都受了重伤。

sentences.en: They were captured and they were taken to a temporary German hospital in a nearby convent,
sentences.zh: 他们被俘虏了，被带到了附近修道院的一家临时德国医院，

sentences.en: German military hospital.
sentences.zh: 德国军事医院。

sentences.en: Now, both of them incredibly managed to escape from the Germans in the night.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们两人竟然奇迹般地在夜里从德国人手中逃脱了。

sentences.en: And they hid in a village where Belgian families took them in.
sentences.zh: 他们躲在一个村子里，比利时家庭收留了他们。

sentences.en: And now they need Edith's help, basically, because they're still injured and they need to get out of Belgium.
sentences.zh: 现在他们基本上需要伊迪丝的帮助，因为他们伤势未愈，需要离开比利时。

sentences.en: And she says, yes, she will help them.
sentences.zh: 她说，是的，她会帮助他们。

sentences.en: This is when Marie has come to ask her, will she do it in principle?

sentences.en: But the German translation made it sound as though she was motivated by eagerness to help the Allies, which is a slightly different thing.
sentences.zh: 但德语翻译让它听起来像是她是因为渴望帮助盟军而受到激励，这是另一回事。

sentences.en: And that's a subtle difference.
sentences.zh: 这是一个微妙的区别。

sentences.en: And that, of course, can mean the difference between life and death.
sentences.zh: 当然，这可能意味着生与死的区别。

sentences.en: I mean, you could be motivated by both, I think.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为你可能两者兼而有之。

sentences.en: And I think she probably is.
sentences.zh: 我想她可能也是这样。

sentences.en: But there's an ambiguity that runs through this story.
sentences.zh: 但这个故事中贯穿着一种模糊性。

sentences.en: Anyway, the important thing is she doesn't make any effort to deny what she's been doing.
sentences.zh: 总之，重要的是她没有试图否认自己的所作所为。

sentences.en: And, in fact, the figures that I quoted earlier for the number of men that she helped to smuggle to safety, they come from her own testimony.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我之前引用的她帮助走私到安全地带的人数，正是来自她自己的证词。

sentences.en: She says to the Germans, I have helped almost 200 men, some of them soldiers, some of them civilians.
sentences.zh: 她对德国人说：我帮助了近200人，其中一些是士兵，一些是平民。

sentences.en: And her biographers and people who have written about this case have often wondered why she was so candid.
sentences.zh: 她的传记作者和写过这个案子的人经常想知道她为什么如此坦诚。

sentences.en: So one explanation is obviously that she's a pious Victorian Christian, and she can't tell a lie.
sentences.zh: 所以一个解释显然是，她是一位虔诚的维多利亚时代基督徒，她不能撒谎。

sentences.en: You know, it's not in her repertoire to be dishoneSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，不诚实从来都不是她的作风。

sentences.en: There's also people who think she's just naive.
sentences.zh: 也有人认为她只是太天真了。

sentences.en: She doesn't realize the gravity of her situation.
sentences.zh: 她没有意识到自己处境的严重性。

sentences.en: And then there are also people who say, well, the Germans told her that the other suspects had already confessed, confessed, and, you know, she was gullible, and she fell for it.
sentences.zh: 还有人说，德国人告诉她其他嫌疑人都已经招供了，而她又轻信了他们，所以才上了当。

sentences.en: And so she thought, well, if the others have confessed, I might as well confess myself.
sentences.zh: 于是她想，既然别人都招了，那我也招了吧。

sentences.en: I think there is definitely an unworldliness to her.
sentences.zh: 我觉得她身上确实有一种与世隔绝的纯真。

sentences.en: I don't think she quite realizes the severity of the situation.
sentences.zh: 我不认为她完全意识到了局势的严峻。

sentences.en: Or do you think perhaps she does, and she is, I mean, prepared to accept a form of martyrdom?
sentences.zh: 还是说你觉得她其实心里清楚，并且已经准备好接受某种殉道了？

sentences.en: We would need to know more about her inner life to get a sense of that.
sentences.zh: 我们需要更了解她的内心世界才能做出判断。

sentences.en: I mean, that's obviously a possibility, that she willingly embraces martyrdom, and she sacrifices herself almost deliberately.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她自愿选择殉道，几乎是刻意牺牲自己，这显然是有可能的。

sentences.en: But that can only be supposition, because we know so little about what's going on behind the sort of, you know, behind the slightly prim nursing facade.
sentences.zh: 但这只能是猜测，因为我们对她那略显刻板的护士外表下究竟在想什么知之甚少。

sentences.en: I mean, she's clearly an unbelievably brave woman.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她显然是一位极其勇敢的女性。

sentences.en: Yeah, and very, very serious and earneSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且非常严肃、非常真诚。

sentences.en: So she describes her time in prison, for example, as a solemn fast from earthly distractions.
sentences.zh: 例如，她将自己在狱中的时光描述为一种远离尘世纷扰的庄严斋戒。

sentences.en: If you're the kind of person who says that about your time in the German prison, then you're not a very, I suspect you're not a very worldly person.
sentences.zh: 如果你会用这种方式来形容自己在德国监狱里的日子，那我怀疑你并不是一个很世俗的人。

sentences.en: Or you're a person who is steeped in the narratives of Christian martyrs, because that's exactly how they talk, you know, in the early martyrologies.
sentences.zh: 或者说，你是一个沉浸在基督教殉道者叙事中的人，因为早期的殉道录里就是这么写的。

sentences.en: Of course, and I think she is.
sentences.zh: 当然，我觉得她就是这样的人。

sentences.en: She grew up in a vicarage, she's a nurse, absolutely, she's part of all that.
sentences.zh: 她在牧师公馆长大，是一名护士，没错，她就是那种背景的人。

sentences.en: I feel that she, you know, she is aware of the script in a situation like this.
sentences.zh: 我觉得她很清楚在这种情况下该扮演什么样的角色。

sentences.en: Yeah, quite possibly, quite possibly.
sentences.zh: 是的，很有可能，很有可能。

sentences.en: I still don't think this makes her a brilliant dinner party companion.
sentences.zh: 但我依然不觉得这让她成了什么有趣的晚宴同伴。

sentences.en: You and I may differ on this.
sentences.zh: 这一点我们可能看法不同。

sentences.en: After 10 weeks in prison, she's taken out on the 2nd of October to face the charges.
sentences.zh: 在狱中待了10周后，她于10月2日被带出来接受指控。

sentences.en: Now, this is not an ordinary court, it is a court-martial.
sentences.zh: 这可不是普通的法庭，而是军事法庭。

sentences.en: And it's a court-martial because she's being charged with war treason under Section 58 of the German military code.
sentences.zh: 之所以是军事法庭，是因为她根据德国军事法典第58条被控犯有战争叛国罪。

sentences.en: And this reads as follows,
sentences.zh: 法典内容如下：

sentences.en: So even if she's English?
sentences.zh: 所以即使她是英国人也一样？

sentences.en: Even if she's English.
sentences.zh: 即使她是英国人也一样。

sentences.en: The code is absolutely explicit about this, that this applies to anybody in the war zone or in the occupation zone.
sentences.zh: 法典对此写得非常明确，适用于任何处于战区或占领区的人。

sentences.en: And her specific offence is conveying troops to the enemy.
sentences.zh: 她具体的罪名是协助敌军运送部队。

sentences.en: Now, later, you see it a lot in accounts of the trial, sort of popular accounts and things.
sentences.zh: 后来，你在很多关于这场审判的记录中，比如通俗读物之类的，经常能看到这一点。

sentences.en: It is described as a show trial.
sentences.zh: 它被描述为一场作秀审判。

sentences.en: It absolutely was not a show trial.
sentences.zh: 但它绝对不是一场作秀审判。

sentences.en: So she has a defence lawyer.
sentences.zh: 所以她是有辩护律师的。

sentences.en: Miss Wilkins chose a lawyer for her who they knew.
sentences.zh: 威尔金斯小姐为她选了一位他们认识的律师。

sentences.en: And the Germans said, no, that person's not right.
sentences.zh: 但德国人说，不行，那个人不合适。

sentences.en: That's just some mate of yours.
sentences.zh: 那不过是你的一位朋友罢了。

sentences.en: So Miss Wilkins is fine.
sentences.zh: 所以威尔金斯小姐没事。

sentences.en: She's off the hook.
sentences.zh: 她脱身了。

sentences.en: Yeah, Miss Wilkins is fine.
sentences.zh: 是的，威尔金斯小姐没事。

sentences.en: But the Germans found her a replacement who was a Brussels lawyer called Sadi Kirshen.
sentences.zh: 但德国人给她找了个替代者，是一位名叫萨迪·基尔申的布鲁塞尔律师。

sentences.en: And there's no suggestion that this defence lawyer let her down or, or, you know, was inadequate or anything like this.
sentences.zh: 没有任何迹象表明这位辩护律师辜负了她，或者表现不力之类的。

sentences.en: Well, it's tricky, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很棘手，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because she's confessed everything.
sentences.zh: 因为她已经全招了。

sentences.en: She doesn't deny the charges.
sentences.zh: 她并不否认指控。

sentences.en: So this is a report by a Belgian official.
sentences.zh: 这是一份比利时官员的报告。

sentences.en: In her oral statement before the court,
sentences.zh: 在法庭上的口头陈述中，

sentences.en: Miss Cavill disclosed almost all the facts of the whole prosecution.
sentences.zh: 卡维尔小姐几乎披露了检方指控的所有事实。

sentences.en: She was questioned in German, an interpreter translating all the questions in French, with which language Miss Cavill was well acquainted.
sentences.zh: 她用德语接受讯问，翻译员将所有问题译成法语，卡维尔小姐对法语非常熟悉。

sentences.en: She spoke without trembling and showed a clear mind.
sentences.zh: 她说话时没有颤抖，头脑清晰。

sentences.en: Often, she added some greater precision to her previous depositions.
sentences.zh: 她还经常对自己之前的证词进行更精确的补充。

sentences.en: When she was asked why she helped these soldiers to go to England, she replied that she thought that if she had not done so, they would have been shot by the Germans,
sentences.zh: 当被问及为何帮助这些士兵前往英国时，她回答说，她认为如果不这样做，他们就会被德国人枪毙，

sentences.en: and that therefore she thought she only did her duty to her country in saving their lives.
sentences.zh: 因此她认为自己挽救他们的生命只是尽了对国家的职责。

sentences.en: But I think it's here that the issue of the translation is so damaging.
sentences.zh: 但我认为正是这一点，翻译问题造成了极大的负面影响。

sentences.en: Because the Germans say, well, hold on.
sentences.zh: 因为德国人会说，等等。

sentences.en: Are you doing this to save their lives?
sentences.zh: 你这么做是为了挽救他们的生命？

sentences.en: Or are you doing this to do your duty to your country?
sentences.zh: 还是为了尽你对国家的职责？

sentences.en: Those are two slightly different things.
sentences.zh: 这两者是有细微差别的。

sentences.en: Are you helping your country?
sentences.zh: 你是在帮助你的国家吗？

sentences.en: Or is this just about pure humanitarianism?
sentences.zh: 还是这纯粹出于人道主义？

sentences.en: Right, because she's saving Belgians as well, isn't she?
sentences.zh: 没错，因为她也在救比利时人，不是吗？

sentences.en: And getting them out to go and join the Allies.
sentences.zh: 并设法让他们出去加入盟军。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the military prosecutor said, but you haven't just helped injured soldiers.
sentences.zh: 所以军事检察官说，但你不仅仅是帮助了受伤的士兵。

sentences.en: You have also helped young Belgians who were not in danger at all, but wanted to get out of the country to join the Allied armies.
sentences.zh: 你还帮助了那些根本没有危险、但想离开国家去加入盟军的年轻比利时人。

sentences.en: You're not saving their lives.
sentences.zh: 你并不是在挽救他们的生命。

sentences.en: You're actually, you know, aiding and abetting them to take up arms against us, against the Germans.
sentences.zh: 你实际上是在教唆他们拿起武器对抗我们，对抗德国人。

sentences.en: And because of that point, it's very hard for them, actually, to pardon her.
sentences.zh: 正因为这一点，他们实际上很难赦免她。

sentences.en: I know this sounds like a massively team Teuton.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来非常像是在为德国人辩护。

sentences.en: Again.
sentences.zh: 又是这样。

sentences.en: The German military code, Tom, is very clear.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，德国军事法典写得很清楚。

sentences.en: I don't know how familiar you are with that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你对它有多了解。

sentences.en: They're only obeying orders.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在执行命令。

sentences.en: Well, the penalty for her crime, right, in the code is death.
sentences.zh: 好吧，法典中她所犯罪行的惩罚是死刑。

sentences.en: And section, you asked about her being foreign.
sentences.zh: 至于你问到的关于她是外国人的问题，

sentences.en: I don't know how familiar you are with section 160 of the German military code, but this explicitly says that in time of war,
sentences.zh: 我不知道你对德国军事法典第160条有多了解，但其中明确规定，在战争时期，

sentences.en: the penalties will apply to foreigners as well as to German nationals.
sentences.zh: 惩罚同样适用于外国人，也适用于德国国民。

sentences.en: Now, you might not want to take this unwelcome news from me, but surely you would take it from Sir Horace Rowland of the Foreign Office.
sentences.zh: 你可能不想从我这里听到这个坏消息，但你肯定会相信外交部的霍勒斯·罗兰爵士吧。

sentences.en: Because Sir Horace Rowland, as we know now from Declassified Files, wrote about this to his colleagues and said, she's in a mess and there's nothing we can do to save her.
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们现在从解密文件中所知，霍勒斯·罗兰爵士曾就此事写信给同事说，她陷入了困境，我们无能为力。

sentences.en: I am afraid it is likely to go hard with Ms. Cavill.
sentences.zh: 恐怕卡维尔小姐的情况不容乐观。

sentences.en: I am afraid we are powerless.
sentences.zh: 恐怕我们无能为力。

sentences.en: Now, he's right.
sentences.zh: 现在看来他是对的。

sentences.en: Because, you know, given the legal framework, conviction is a foregone conclusion.
sentences.zh: 因为在法律框架下，定罪是必然的结果。

sentences.en: And a couple of days later, on the afternoon of Monday, the 11th of October, the sentences are handed down.
sentences.zh: 几天后，即10月11日星期一下午，判决下达了。

sentences.en: So nine people are found guilty.
sentences.zh: 九人被判有罪。

sentences.en: Four of them are sentenced to hard labour.
sentences.zh: 其中四人被判处苦役。

sentences.en: Five of them are condemned to death.
sentences.zh: 五人被判处死刑。

sentences.en: And the people who are condemned to death are Edith Cavill, this bloke Bauch, the architect,
sentences.zh: 被判处死刑的人是伊迪丝·卡维尔、那个叫鲍赫的建筑师，

sentences.en: the schoolteacher, Thulier, who was helping him, and two other people.
sentences.zh: 还有帮助他的教师图利耶，以及另外两人。

sentences.en: I mean, the princess gets off, doesn't she?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那位公主逃脱了惩罚，对吧？

sentences.en: She gets off, exactly.
sentences.zh: 她确实逃脱了，没错。

sentences.en: And she then pops up in the Second World War doing exactly the same thing.
sentences.zh: 而且她在二战中又冒了出来，干着同样的事情。

sentences.en: She's a very impressive woman.
sentences.zh: 她是一位非常了不起的女性。

sentences.en: She can't get enough of it.
sentences.zh: 她对此乐此不疲。

sentences.en: Thulier, the schoolteacher, and two of the others are given reprieves.
sentences.zh: 图利耶老师和其他两人获得了缓刑。

sentences.en: But Philippe Boeck and Edith Cavill are seen as the worst offenders.
sentences.zh: 但菲利普·博克和伊迪丝·卡维尔被视为最严重的罪犯。

sentences.en: Edith, because she has confessed and made such a sort of, she's made no secret about what she's done.
sentences.zh: 伊迪丝是因为她已经招供，而且对于自己的所作所为毫不掩饰。

sentences.en: And she's unrepentant.
sentences.zh: 而且她毫无悔意。

sentences.en: And she's unrepentant.
sentences.zh: 她毫无悔意。

sentences.en: And as a result of this, she is sentenced to death by firing squad.
sentences.zh: 因此，她被判处行刑队枪决。

sentences.en: And the German military commander in Brussels, who has the excellent name,
sentences.zh: 布鲁塞尔的德国军事指挥官，名字非常响亮，

sentences.en: General Traugott von Saubertsweig, he says, I want the sentence carried out straight away, because otherwise there's going to be a massive hullabaloo.
sentences.zh: 特劳戈特·冯·萨伯茨威格将军，他说，我要求立即执行判决，否则会引起轩然大波。

sentences.en: Like, come on, we're not going to have a massive faff and a back and forth about this.
sentences.zh: 就像是，别闹了，我们可不想为了这事儿搞得大费周章、反复拉扯。

sentences.en: Let's just get this done.
sentences.zh: 赶紧办完吧。

sentences.en: So that very night, 11th of October, the German Lutheran chaplain of the prison, who's called Paul Le Ser, who you quoted at the beginning,
sentences.zh: 于是就在那天晚上，10月11日，你开头引用的那位监狱德国路德宗牧师保罗·勒塞尔，

sentences.en: he comes to see Edith and he says to her, you're going to be shot at dawn.
sentences.zh: 他来见伊迪丝并告诉她，你将在黎明时分被枪决。

sentences.en: And he describes it.
sentences.zh: 他描述了当时的情景。

sentences.en: For one moment, her cheeks were flushed and a moist film passed over her eyes, but only for a few seconds.
sentences.zh: 有一瞬间，她的脸颊泛红，双眼蒙上一层湿润的薄膜，但只持续了几秒钟。

sentences.en: I offered her my services as a pastor, and I stated that I was at her disposal any hour of the day and night, but she declined it politely, but definitely.
sentences.zh: 我提出为她提供牧师服务，并表示我随时听候差遣，但她礼貌而坚定地拒绝了。

sentences.en: And then this bloke, Le Ser, says to her, can I not offer you some kindness?
sentences.zh: 然后这个叫勒塞尔的家伙对她说，我能为你做点什么吗？

sentences.en: Please do not see in me now the German, but only the servant of our Lord and Saviour, who places himself entirely at your disposal.
sentences.zh: 请不要把我当成德国人，只把我当成我们主和救世主的仆人，我完全听候你的差遣。

sentences.en: And she says,
sentences.zh: 她说，

sentences.en: well, okay, fine.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那行。

sentences.en: Could you get word of what's happened to my mother?
sentences.zh: 你能帮我传个话，告诉我母亲发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: My mother is 80 and she's back in Norwich, and I don't want my mom to hear about this in the newspapers.
sentences.zh: 我母亲80岁了，住在诺里奇，我不想让她从报纸上得知这件事。

sentences.en: And he says, I will.
sentences.zh: 他说，我会的。

sentences.en: And actually, he says in his account, I kept my promise.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他在记录中说，我信守了诺言。

sentences.en: I don't know how they, they must have sent a message somehow to the British.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他们是怎么做的，他们一定通过某种方式给英国人发了消息。

sentences.en: Telegram or something.
sentences.zh: 电报之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: And then he makes a pretty big offer to her, I think.
sentences.zh: 然后我觉得他向她提出了一个非常重要的提议。

sentences.en: He says, I know that you're, you know, very pious and you're a big Christian, and I know you'll want to take communion before you die,
sentences.zh: 他说，我知道你非常虔诚，是一位坚定的基督徒，我知道你死前会想领圣餐，

sentences.en: but I know you also will find it difficult if it's coming from, and this is from his account, a German in the uniform, which she doubtless hated.
sentences.zh: 但我知道，如果这圣餐是由——这是他记录中的话——一个穿着她无疑非常痛恨的德国军服的人提供，你会感到为难。

sentences.en: And he says, I know the Anglican chaplain in Brussels, who you also know, who's a guy called Reverend Sterling Gahan, and I'll bring him to your cell.
sentences.zh: 他说，我认识布鲁塞尔的英国国教牧师，你也认识他，他叫斯特林·加汉牧师，我会带他来你的牢房。

sentences.en: And he says, her eyes lighted up, and with great joy, she accepted.
sentences.zh: 他说，她的眼睛亮了起来，并欣然接受了。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: I've got to say, everyone is behaving very well.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，每个人的表现都非常得体。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And this bloke, the Reverend Sterling Gahan, he arrives later that evening.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上晚些时候，斯特林·加汉牧师到了。

sentences.en: He already knew her.
sentences.zh: 他本来就认识她。

sentences.en: The German authorities said, fine, you know, you can come.
sentences.zh: 德国当局说，行，你可以去。

sentences.en: He finds this very, very emotional.
sentences.zh: 他感到非常非常激动。

sentences.en: To my astonishment and relief, I found my friend perfectly calm and resigned, but this could not lessen the tenderness and intensity of feeling on either part.
sentences.zh: 令我惊讶和宽慰的是，我发现我的朋友非常平静和顺从，但这并不能减轻双方心中那份温柔与强烈的情感。

sentences.en: And she says to this bloke, please tell all my friends that I willingly gave, my life for my country.
sentences.zh: 她对他说，请告诉我的所有朋友，我甘愿为国捐躯。

sentences.en: I've seen death so often, it's not strange or fearful to me.
sentences.zh: 我见过太多次死亡，它对我来说并不陌生，也不可怕。

sentences.en: And there's some very famous lines, which end up being on their statue.
sentences.zh: 还有几句非常著名的话，最终被刻在了她的雕像上。

sentences.en: They have all been very kind to me here, but this I would say, standing as I do in view of God and eternity, I realize that patriotism is not enough.
sentences.zh: 他们在这里对我都很友善，但我必须说，站在上帝和永恒的视角下，我意识到爱国是不够的。

sentences.en: I must have no hatred or bitterness towards anyone.
sentences.zh: 我对任何人都不应有仇恨或怨恨。

sentences.en: And then they pray, they take communion together, and they talk quietly until the guards tell him it's time to go.
sentences.zh: 然后他们一起祈祷，领了圣餐，并静静地交谈，直到守卫告诉他该走了。

sentences.en: He says later, I said goodbye.
sentences.zh: 他后来写道，我说了再见。

sentences.en: And she smiled and said, we shall meet again.
sentences.zh: 她微笑着说，我们会再见的。

sentences.en: And then when he's gone, she writes a farewell letter to her nurses, very moving letter, actually.
sentences.zh: 他走后，她给她的护士们写了一封告别信，那封信真的很感人。

sentences.en: When better days come, our work will again grow and resume all its power for doing good.
sentences.zh: 当更好的日子到来时，我们的工作将再次成长，并恢复其行善的所有力量。

sentences.en: I told you that devotion would bring you true happiness, and that the thought that before God, you've done your duty well and with a good heart,
sentences.zh: 我告诉过你们，奉献会给你们带来真正的幸福，而那种在上帝面前，你们已经尽职尽责、问心无愧的想法，

sentences.en: will sustain you in the hard moments of life and in the face of death.
sentences.zh: 将在你们人生的艰难时刻和面对死亡时支撑着你们。

sentences.en: I may have been strict, but I have loved you more than you can know.
sentences.zh: 我可能很严厉，但我对你们的爱超过你们的想象。

sentences.en: Oh, very sad.
sentences.zh: 哦，太令人难过了。

sentences.en: Now overnight, while she's doing all this, there is a chance of a lifeline.
sentences.zh: 就在她做这一切的当晚，还有一线生机。

sentences.en: And this comes from the Americans.
sentences.zh: 这来自美国人。

sentences.en: People who listened to the last episode will recall that despite the sinking of the Lusitania, the Americans have still not entered the war,
sentences.zh: 听过上一集的人会记得，尽管发生了卢西塔尼亚号沉没事件，美国人仍然没有参战，

sentences.en: and the Germans are keen not to antagonize them.
sentences.zh: 而德国人非常不想激怒他们。

sentences.en: And the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而美国

sentences.en: ambassador in Brussels, of course he has a U.S.
sentences.zh: 驻布鲁塞尔大使，当然他有一位美国

sentences.en: ambassador's name.
sentences.zh: 大使的名字。

sentences.en: He is called Brand Whitlock.
sentences.zh: 他叫布兰德·惠特洛克。

sentences.en: And Brand Whitlock sends the German governor general a note asking him for mercy.
sentences.zh: 布兰德·惠特洛克给德国总督发了一份照会，请求他开恩。

sentences.en: And he says, her career,
sentences.zh: 他说，她的职业，

sentences.en: Miss Cavill's career as a servant of humanity, is such as to inspire the greatest sympathy and to call for pardon.
sentences.zh: 卡维尔小姐作为人类仆人的职业，足以激发最大的同情并值得赦免。

sentences.en: And Brand Whitlock, he's actually ill that evening.
sentences.zh: 而布兰德·惠特洛克那天晚上其实病了。

sentences.en: He can't be bothered to go himself.
sentences.zh: 他没法亲自去。

sentences.en: So he sends a delegation from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以他从美国大使馆派出了一个代表团，

sentences.en: embassy, and indeed some Spaniards, who are also neutral.
sentences.zh: 事实上还有一些同样保持中立的西班牙人。

sentences.en: And they go to see the governor.
sentences.zh: 他们去见总督。

sentences.en: And at the head of this is a diplomat called Hugh Gibson,
sentences.zh: 带头的是一位名叫休·吉布森的外交官，

sentences.en: American diplomat.
sentences.zh: 美国外交官。

sentences.en: And he says, we reminded him of the burning of Louvain and of the sinking of the Lusitania.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们提醒了他鲁汶的焚毁和卢西塔尼亚号的沉没。

sentences.en: And we told him, this is the German governor, that this murder would rank with those two affairs and would stir all civilized countries with horror and disguSt.
sentences.zh: 我们告诉他，这是德国总督，这次谋杀将与那两起事件相提并论，并会引起所有文明国家的惊恐和厌恶。

sentences.en: And one day, a podcast series, we'll do them in succession.
sentences.zh: 有一天，我们会做一个播客系列，连续讲述这些故事。

sentences.en: Exactly, as we did.
sentences.zh: 没错，就像我们做过的那样。

sentences.en: And at that, one of the German officials, who's called Count Harak, interrupts.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，一位名叫哈拉克伯爵的德国官员插话了。

sentences.en: And he says, hold on, hold on.
sentences.zh: 他说，等等，等等。

sentences.en: I would rather see Miss Cavill shot than see any harm come to the humblest German soldier.
sentences.zh: 我宁愿看到卡维尔小姐被枪决，也不愿看到最卑微的德国士兵受到任何伤害。

sentences.en: My only regret is that we don't have three or four more old English women to shoot.
sentences.zh: 我唯一的遗憾是我们没有更多三四个这样的英国老太婆可以枪毙。

sentences.en: Well, they've got Miss Wilkins.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们还有威尔金斯小姐。

sentences.en: Yeah, they could shoot.
sentences.zh: 是啊，他们本可以枪毙她。

sentences.en: Why aren't they shooting Miss Wilkins?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们不枪毙威尔金斯小姐呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, she's the one that got away, no?
sentences.zh: 是啊，她是那个逃脱的人，不是吗？

sentences.en: She is.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: The Americans were really shocked by this.
sentences.zh: 美国人对此感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: So this bloke,
sentences.zh: 所以这个家伙，

sentences.en: Gibson went back and wrote it down and said, which is terrible form from the Germans.
sentences.zh: 吉布森回去后写了下来，说这在德国人看来是非常糟糕的举动。

sentences.en: Is it a joke?
sentences.zh: 这是一个玩笑吗？

sentences.en: I think it's obviously a joke.
sentences.zh: 我认为这显然是个玩笑。

sentences.en: It's German banter.
sentences.zh: 这是德国式的调侃。

sentences.en: Very Wagnerian quip.
sentences.zh: 非常瓦格纳式的俏皮话。

sentences.en: It's Wagnerian banter.
sentences.zh: 这是瓦格纳式的调侃。

sentences.en: Plus, the Germans have been woken up at like one in the morning by this group of people who aren't even in the war.
sentences.zh: 况且，德国人凌晨一点左右被这群甚至没参战的人吵醒了。

sentences.en: I think this bloke's just like, come on, leave us alone.
sentences.zh: 我想这家伙只是觉得，拜托，别烦我们了。

sentences.en: We're just, you know, we're not following orders.
sentences.zh: 我们只是，你知道，我们没有违抗命令。

sentences.en: They're just following the German military code.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在执行德国军事法典。

sentences.en: Yeah,
sentences.zh: 是啊，

sentences.en: I'm glad that's very, very clear.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴这一点非常、非常清楚。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So now we come to the early hours of the 12th of October.
sentences.zh: 现在我们来到10月12日的凌晨。

sentences.en: And there are different accounts of what happened, but the most reliable is from that Lutheran pastor,
sentences.zh: 关于当时发生的事情有不同的说法，但最可靠的是来自那位路德教牧师，

sentences.en: Paul the Sir.
sentences.zh: 勒瑟尔。

sentences.en: It's very evocative.
sentences.zh: 这非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: And that scene that you described, so he goes to the prison.
sentences.zh: 正如你描述的那个场景，他去了监狱。

sentences.en: And she's been kneeling at her table.
sentences.zh: 她一直跪在桌边。

sentences.en: He's told she's been kneeling in prayer and he goes into the cell and she's packed up all her stuff.
sentences.zh: 有人告诉他她一直在跪着祈祷，他走进牢房，她已经收拾好了所有的东西。

sentences.en: And there's just a little sort of flame burning gas flame.
sentences.zh: 只有一盏小小的煤气灯在燃烧。

sentences.en: And she's got, she's got ready.
sentences.zh: 她已经准备好了。

sentences.en: The two of them go out of the cell and they walk through the silent corridors of the prison.
sentences.zh: 他们两人走出牢房，穿过监狱寂静的走廊。

sentences.en: The scene that you described at the beginning, the Belgian prison guards have all lined up to sort of wish her well.
sentences.zh: 你开头描述的那个场景，比利时狱警们都排成一列，算是为她送行。

sentences.en: And as Le Sœur says, they greeted her silently with the highest respect.
sentences.zh: 正如勒瑟尔所说，他们默默地向她致以最高的敬意。

sentences.en: So they get into a car and then the Catholic chaplain comes out of the prison with Philippe Boek.
sentences.zh: 他们上了车，然后天主教随军牧师和菲利普·博克一起从监狱里出来。

sentences.en: He gets into a car.
sentences.zh: 他上了一辆车。

sentences.en: He also behaves splendidly.
sentences.zh: 他的表现也非常出色。

sentences.en: Philippe Boek, he says to all the German censors in Dutch, he says, let us bear no grudge.
sentences.zh: 菲利普·博克用荷兰语对所有的德国审查员说，让我们不要怀恨在心。

sentences.en: And then he gets into the car and they drive off.
sentences.zh: 然后他上了车，他们开车离开了。

sentences.en: And they drive to the Tien Nationale, which is the national shooting range, which is where the Germans usually hold their executions.
sentences.zh: 他们开车前往国家射击场，那是德国人通常执行死刑的地方。

sentences.en: And there a company of 250 German soldiers is lined up waiting for them.
sentences.zh: 在那里，一个由250名德国士兵组成的连队排成一列等着他们。

sentences.en: They present arMs.
sentences.zh: 他们举枪致敬。

sentences.en: Edith and this architect Boek are led to the front.
sentences.zh: 伊迪丝和这位建筑师博克被带到前面。

sentences.en: And the sentences are read out in French and German.
sentences.zh: 判决书用法语和德语宣读。

sentences.en: Boek cries out at this point.
sentences.zh: 博克此时大喊起来。

sentences.en: He says, comrades in the presence of death, we are all comrades.
sentences.zh: 他说，同志们，在死亡面前，我们都是同志。

sentences.en: And then someone says, pipe down, you know, stop talking.
sentences.zh: 然后有人说，闭嘴，你知道，别说话了。

sentences.en: Le Sœur, the Lutheran is allowed a last word with Edith.
sentences.zh: 路德教牧师勒瑟尔获准与伊迪丝做最后的告别。

sentences.en: And he sort of presses her hand.
sentences.zh: 他握了握她的手。

sentences.en: And he says to her in English, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ and the love of God and the communion of the Holy Ghost be with you forever.
sentences.zh: 他用英语对她说，愿我们主耶稣基督的恩惠，上帝的慈爱，圣灵的团契，永远与你同在。

sentences.en: Amen.
sentences.zh: 阿门。

sentences.en: And she says, ask Mr. Gahan to tell my loved ones later that my soul as I believe is safe and that I'm glad to die for my country.
sentences.zh: 她说，请转告加汉先生，告诉我的亲人们，我相信我的灵魂是安全的，我很高兴为国捐躯。

sentences.en: And then she's led to the pole.
sentences.zh: 然后她被带到柱子前。

sentences.en: She's loosely tied to this pole.
sentences.zh: 她被松松地绑在柱子上。

sentences.en: A bandage is put over her eyes, which the Sœur says, as the soldier who put it on told me, were full of tears.
sentences.zh: 她的眼睛被蒙上绷带，勒瑟尔说，正如给她蒙上绷带的士兵告诉我的，那双眼睛里满是泪水。

sentences.en: And then a few seconds passed, which appeared to me like eternity.
sentences.zh: 接着过了几秒钟，在我看来就像永恒一样。

sentences.en: Immediately the sharp commands were given.
sentences.zh: 紧接着发出了尖锐的命令。

sentences.en: Two salvos crashed at the same time.
sentences.zh: 两轮齐射同时响起。

sentences.en: Each of eight men at a distance of six paces.
sentences.zh: 每轮八人，距离六步。

sentences.en: And the two condemned persons sank to the ground without a sound.
sentences.zh: 两名死刑犯倒在地上，没有发出任何声音。

sentences.en: Now that makes it sound as though it's all very clean and very clinical, but actually that's not the case.
sentences.zh: 这听起来好像一切都很干净、很专业，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: The Sœur goes on to say, my eyes were fixed exclusively on Miss Cavill and what they now saw was terrible.
sentences.zh: 勒瑟尔接着说，我的目光一直盯着卡维尔小姐，我所看到的景象太可怕了。

sentences.en: With a face streaming with blood, one shot had gone through her forehead.
sentences.zh: 她的脸血流如注，一颗子弹穿过了她的前额。

sentences.en: Miss Cavill had sunk down forwards, but three times she raised herself up without a sound with her hands stretched upwards.
sentences.zh: 卡维尔小姐向前倒下，但她三次无声地抬起身体，双手向上伸展。

sentences.en: And he runs forward with the doctor and the doctor says to him, don't worry, these are just the sort of last automatic reflexes before death.
sentences.zh: 他跑过去和医生在一起，医生对他说，别担心，这只是死亡前最后的自动反射。

sentences.en: And then she does die.
sentences.zh: 然后她真的去世了。

sentences.en: And the Sœur said, the bullet holes as large as a fist in the back proved without any doubt that she was killed immediately.
sentences.zh: 勒瑟尔说，背部拳头大小的弹孔毫无疑问地证明她是当场死亡的。

sentences.en: I only mentioned this fact because untrue rumours have been connected with it.
sentences.zh: 我提到这个事实只是因为一些不实的谣言与此有关。

sentences.en: We will come back to these rumours.
sentences.zh: 我们会回到这些谣言上来。

sentences.en: So keep these rumours in your heads.
sentences.zh: 所以请记住这些谣言。

sentences.en: Then a few minutes later, he says, the coffins were lowered into the graves and I prayed over Edith Cavill's grave and I invoked the Lord's blessing over her poor corpse.
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，他说，棺材被放入墓穴，我在伊迪丝·卡维尔的墓前祈祷，并祈求上帝保佑她可怜的遗体。

sentences.en: Then I went home, almost sick in my soul.
sentences.zh: 然后我回家了，灵魂几乎感到恶心。

sentences.en: So this is just one death, or two deaths if you include the architect, against the backdrop of a war in which thousands of people are dying every month
sentences.zh: 这只是一次死亡，如果算上那位建筑师就是两次，而背景是一场每个月都有成千上万人在死亡的战争，

sentences.en: on the Western and Eastern fronts.
sentences.zh: 在西线和东线。

sentences.en: But it becomes a massive story on both sides of the Atlantic because Edith Cavill is turned immediately into a martyr, into an innocent victim of German barbarism.
sentences.zh: 但它在大西洋两岸都成为了一个巨大的新闻，因为伊迪丝·卡维尔立即被塑造成了一位烈士，德国野蛮行径的无辜受害者。

sentences.en: So to quote Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, who is very enthusiastically pouring out propaganda for the British government at this point, everybody must feel disgusted
sentences.zh: 引用阿瑟·柯南·道尔爵士的话，他当时正非常热心地为英国政府散布宣传，每个人都必须感到厌恶，

sentences.en: at the barbarous actions of the German soldiery in murdering this great and glorious specimen of womanhood.
sentences.zh: 对德国士兵谋杀这位伟大而光荣的女性典范的野蛮行径。

sentences.en: The New York Herald.
sentences.zh: 《纽约先驱报》。

sentences.en: The official report received today will cause a wave of horror to sweep over the world at the thought of the possibility of a nation which will perpetrate such a terrible thing
sentences.zh: 今天收到的官方报告将引发全球范围内的惊恐，人们想到一个犯下如此可怕罪行的国家，

sentences.en: succeeding in this war and dominating Europe.
sentences.zh: 竟然能在战争中获胜并统治欧洲。

sentences.en: And basically the newspaper goes on to say, you know, the thought of the Germans winning must be complete anathema to any democratic American having read this story.
sentences.zh: 基本上报纸接着说，你知道，任何读过这个故事的民主美国人，想到德国人获胜一定会感到完全的厌恶。

sentences.en: And the funny thing, of course, is that nobody up to this point had ever heard of Edith Cavill.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，当然，在此之前没人听说过伊迪丝·卡维尔。

sentences.en: It's not like she's a celebrity or something.
sentences.zh: 她又不是什么名人。

sentences.en: But in a way that works brilliantly because it means that she's a blank slate and people can project onto her this sort of idealized portrait of a kind of Christian womanhood.
sentences.zh: 但在某种程度上，这反而效果极佳，因为这意味着她是一张白纸，人们可以将那种理想化的基督教女性形象投射到她身上。

sentences.en: She's a nurse.
sentences.zh: 她是一名护士。

sentences.en: So her kind of white uniform and the red cross on it and perfect.
sentences.zh: 所以她那白色的制服和上面的红十字，非常完美。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the British War Propaganda Bureau, which was operating to spread the word in America, takes her story and it puts it alongside the Belgian atrocities and the Lusitania
sentences.zh: 因此，负责在美国传播消息的英国战争宣传局，利用她的故事，将其与比利时暴行和卢西塔尼亚号事件并列，

sentences.en: in the sort of chamber of horrors of German crimes.
sentences.zh: 放入德国罪行的恐怖陈列室中。

sentences.en: And the newspapers, both in America and in Britain, print ever more lurid accounts of her final moments.
sentences.zh: 美国和英国的报纸都刊登了关于她最后时刻越来越耸人听闻的报道。

sentences.en: So this is what Le Sœur was talking about when he said about untrue rumours.
sentences.zh: 这就是勒瑟尔提到不实谣言时所指的内容。

sentences.en: So there were stories that German soldiers refused to fire on her and that the officers had to do it.
sentences.zh: 当时有传言说德国士兵拒绝向她开枪，军官不得不亲自下手。

sentences.en: Or the most common story, that she'd fainted before the firing squad and then an officer stood over her with his revolver pressed against her head
sentences.zh: 或者最常见的说法是，她在行刑队前昏倒了，然后一名军官站在她身边，用左轮手枪抵住她的头，

sentences.en: and basically blew her brains out.
sentences.zh: 直接把她的脑浆打出来了。

sentences.en: I mean, this is not true, but it becomes, again, a little bit like the stories that we talked about last time about German schoolchildren being given the day off
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不是真的，但这又变得有点像我们上次谈到的关于德国小学生被放假一天，

sentences.en: to celebrate the sinking of the Lusitania.
sentences.zh: 去庆祝卢西塔尼亚号沉没的故事一样。

sentences.en: It becomes a widely accepted urban legend.
sentences.zh: 它变成了一个广为流传的都市传说。

sentences.en: And you can find, you know, you can see them online,
sentences.zh: 你可以找到，你知道，你可以在网上看到，

sentences.en: loads of examples of posters and postcards about the execution of Edith Cavill.
sentences.zh: 大量关于伊迪丝·卡维尔被处决的海报和明信片的例子。

sentences.en: They always show her in a nurse's uniform, which she would not have worn at the execution, marked with a big red cross.
